unit: per job: the intake manifold gasket set for one engine, with the manifold removed and refitted. Which gaskets are in the set differs by engine and is stated per example: a single set of port gaskets on a four-cylinder; upper (manifold or plenum) gaskets and, where noted, the lower (manifold base to cylinder head) gaskets on a V6; the manifold-to-head set on a V8. finding: The live range of $490-$1,275 is too high at the bottom for modern engines and about right at the top only for engines with a buried or two-piece manifold. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Honda Fit about $218-$366 (1.6-2.0 hr); midsize 2016 Honda Pilot about $137-$393 (0.8-1.8 hr); truck 2013 Silverado 1500 5.3L about $178-$479 (0.9-2.0 hr); luxury 2016 Acura MDX about $331-$482 (1.8-2.0 hr). Every one of these sits below the live floor of $490. The gaskets themselves are cheap ($26-$160 for a set on the listings seen) and on these engines the plastic manifold comes off in one to two hours. Three of the five benchmarks start at $300-$350 (CarParts.com, AutoZone, Jerry), and YourMechanic's figure for a 2015 F-150 5.0L is $463, so a floor of roughly $250-$350 is better supported than $490; our own lowest totals are lower still because they use warranty times and online parts prices. RepairPal's $683-$834 is higher mainly because its parts figure ($370-$375) is several times the price of any gasket set found. The $1,275 top is not reached by any of our examples, but it is plausible for harder engines: the general guide used here gives 2 to 6 hours, a GM bulletin gives 6.3-6.7 hours just to change the intake manifold on the 3.0L diesel trucks, and Jerry's range runs past $2,000. Those engines are not represented in our four classes, so the top is neither confirmed nor contradicted by a built total. How solid the labor times are: none is a manufacturer time for exactly 'replace intake manifold gaskets'. The Pilot low end (0.8 hr) is Honda's warranty time to replace the upper intake manifold on that vehicle, which uses the same six gaskets. The Fit time (1.6 hr) is Honda's time for an intake-port carbon cleaning that removes the manifold, and the MDX time (1.8 hr) is Acura's time for a fuel pump replacement that removes both the manifold and its base; both include extra work, so they overstate the gasket job slightly while still being warranty times. The truck low end (0.9 hr) is for a comparable V8 in a Dodge Charger, not the Silverado, and its high end is a parts seller's approximate 2 hours for the Silverado. The 2-hour high end for the Fit and MDX is the bottom of a general 2-to-6-hour statement, chosen by us because the manufacturer times are below it. On parts, no clearly priced aftermarket set was found for the Pilot or MDX, so their low ends are discounted genuine gaskets, and the GM kit price comes from a GMC Yukon catalog page for the same 5.3L engine family. Second look (2026-11-20): no numbers were changed. A further search of maker bulletins (Honda, Acura, GM, FCA, Ford, Toyota, Kia, Subaru) found no labor operation for replacing intake manifold gaskets alone on any of the four examples, and none at all for the Silverado. The only additions are two cross-checks: FCA's 1.0 hr to inspect and replace the intake manifold on a 2022-2023 Dodge Durango 5.7L V8, which agrees with the 0.9 hr Charger figure used for the truck low end, and Honda's 2.2 hr valve adjustment on the 2021-22 Pilot, which begins by removing the same upper manifold. What is still weak, stated precisely: the Fit low end (1.6 hr) and the MDX low end (1.8 hr) are times for larger jobs (port cleaning; a fuel pump swap) and so overstate the gasket work; the Pilot high end (1.8 hr) is that same Acura fuel-pump time on a different vehicle; the Pilot low end (0.8 hr) is for replacing the manifold and a PCV hose rather than the gaskets alone; the truck low end is another maker's V8; and the 2-hour high ends for the Fit, MDX and Silverado are a general statement or a seller's approximation. Treat every hour figure here as indicative, not as a book time for this job.
extras: A quote often adds diagnosis (a smoke test for a vacuum leak, or a coolant pressure test on engines where coolant runs through the intake), a throttle body gasket and EGR gaskets, fuel injector seals, shop supplies and sales tax. On engines with coolant passages in the intake, add new coolant and often a thermostat. Shops may suggest cleaning carbon from the intake ports or throttle body while the manifold is off, and spark plugs on V6 engines where the rear bank is only reachable with the manifold removed. If the manifold itself is cracked or warped it is replaced, which costs far more than the gaskets.
